analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Semis roll on sentiment & competition; Meta Muse Wonder; PUB solid; CTS Eventim initiation; Andrej Karpathy
key_insights: Global equities weakened as investors de-risked from AI-capex and AI-financing exposure. QQQ fell 0.7% in low holiday volumes and Asia's MSCI benchmark fell 1.7%, while megacaps held up better: Meta +3.4%, Apple +1.3%, Microsoft +1.0%.

Semis and optical names (CIEN, LITE) bore the brunt of the sell-off. Kospi fell 6.2% on concerns over the durability and financing of the AI buildout, higher borrowing costs and potential Chinese memory competition (CXMT progress on a new memory architecture got much of the blame).
The desk sees nervousness ahead of an Anthropic S-1 as a factor in the AI-exposure de-risking.

Meta launched Muse Wonder, a frontier model reported to rank behind only Claude Opus 5.5 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index. It scored 57.5% on SWE-Marathon vs 46.3% for Opus 5.5 and is priced at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens. It will power Meta's Muse personal agent and be sold directly to businesses, reinforcing Zuckerberg's commitment to higher AI spending.
Microsoft unveiled the Maia 300 custom AI chip, mainly for AI inference from 2027. The longer-term implication is lower dependence on Nvidia and better power efficiency.

Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said capital may now be a bigger constraint than chips or power. He said wafer and memory shortages are easing and compute demand exceeds supply, likely through 2028-29 and potentially into 2030. The desk says the press focused on his negative comments on investors and took them out of context.

Hock Tan called OpenAI's ~$50 billion annualised revenue (as of September) evidence of real demand and a viable business model, while saying a lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in, especially in frontier LLM funding.

PUB reported Q4 organic growth of 5% vs sell-side at 4.8%, but the desk thinks the buyside expected above 5%. Sapient improved sequentially and PUB now guides Sapient to turn positive globally in Q4 vs the Street at about -2%, implying Q4 at the higher end of the 4.5%-5% range. North America missed, implying softer media.
PUB positioning has cleaned up: it screened among the 10 biggest increases in market-value dollars of shorts last week on GS prime brokerage. The call is at 830.

CTS Eventim: GS initiates at Neutral. Valuation is near trough after a roughly 50% de-rating. Concerns are slowing growth, stronger competition from Live Nation and whether venue expansion creates value while staying capital-light. November's Capital Markets Day is the key near-term catalyst.

Andrej Karpathy describes a widening funnel of understanding of LLM capability: about 6 billion people have barely used these systems, 1-2 billion use free-tier chatbots, about 20 million professionals see weeks-long projects collapse into agent work, and about 5,000 people with internal frontier access see agent swarms tackling megaprojects at speeds that outpace human review.

Banking regulators including the Federal Reserve are questioning banks on advanced AI models and agentic-AI safeguards, while the Bank of England and ECB push banks to strengthen recovery plans over cyberattack and rogue-agent concerns (Reuters).

Anthropic said experiments suggest small models could be months away from autonomously replicating across poorly secured IoT devices (Reuters). Anthropic also said new safeguards cut reasoning data harvested in distillation attacks by 90% to 99%.

GS Global Tech Semis Memory: high-bandwidth flash (HBF) and other NAND-based solutions could address a worsening memory constraint in AI inference. GS sees a TAM of about $40-150B at 15%-50% GPU adoption by 2030 and about 30% lower overall inference throughput cost. GS favours SanDisk (Buy), SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics (Buy), and sees Micron (Neutral) as less of a direct beneficiary.

GS Americas Payment Tech Q3 preview is broadly positive: spending volumes remain robust, regulatory and disruption risks are fading, agentic commerce is emerging as a growth driver, and the group is cheap vs history. GS highlights V, MA, TOST and GLBE, is more constructive into earnings on V, MA, PYPL, GLBE and RSKD, and more cautious on FIS, FISV and FOUR.

Q3 global smartphone shipments fell 20% y/y to the lowest since 2012 as AI infrastructure demand tightened memory supply. Gartner says PC shipments fell 22.4% to 55.4 million units, with DRAM costs up fivefold y/y in Q2.

NVIDIA introduced pluggable modules developed with Cisco, which may be adopted by major CSPs and could push growth for Taiwan optical module suppliers Luxnet and PCL. NVIDIA also unveiled its Vera Rubin CPU and MGX 1.2 rack architecture at OCP.
Sage Q3 preview: 4Q organic recurring revenue growth around 10% and FY27 guidance likely to bracket consensus. Small estimate changes cut EPS forecasts by about 1%.

Nokia is selling its Enterprise Campus Edge business to Aurelius, closing in H1-27. Orange Spain is seeking Huawei refund protection if Europe bans Chinese telecom equipment under the proposed EU Cybersecurity Act, expected in early 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Hock Tan says compute demand exceeds supply through 2028-29 and possibly 2030, and OpenAI's ~$50 billion annualised revenue shows real demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital and its cost are becoming the bigger constraint. Kospi fell 6.2% on financing durability and higher borrowing costs, and Tan said many investors do not know what they are investing in.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An Anthropic S-1 or other financing event that shows weak funding appetite for frontier labs would support the bear case.
